08:00 Visit log

Thirty minutes at your pool, line by line

  1. 08:02

    Skim and brush

    Leaves, pollen and storm debris come off the surface first. Then the walls, steps and waterline tile get brushed so the chlorine can reach them.

  2. 08:09

    Test the water

    pH, free chlorine, alkalinity and stabilizer read on site, from water drawn at elbow depth, away from the return jets.

  3. 08:15

    Balance it

    Only what the readings call for goes in: chlorine, acid or stabilizer. Each one is written on your report with the amount.

  4. 08:22

    Baskets and pressure

    Skimmer and pump baskets emptied. Filter pressure read on the gauge. If it is high, the cartridge gets cleaned or the sand gets backwashed.

08:24 The tile line, where scale and algae show first.

Water check Sample report

Nothing ticked yet. Each sign you tick prints here with its cause, first action and a sample price.

Cloudy or milky

Likely cause
Low chlorine after rain, or a dirty filter.
First action
Test, shock, clean the cartridge.
Sample price
$350–$900 per job

Green or slimy walls

Likely cause
Chlorine dropped long enough for algae to hold on.
First action
Brush every wall and step, shock, run the filter until it clears.
Sample price
$350–$900 per job

Strong chlorine smell

Likely cause
Used-up chlorine (chloramines), not too much of it.
First action
Test free and total chlorine, then shock to burn it off.
Sample price
$140–$190 per month, weekly

Foam or scum line

Likely cause
Sunscreen, oils or pollen sitting at the tile.
First action
Skim, wipe the waterline tile, check the filter pressure.
Sample price
$120–$200 per cleaning
